scientific_integrity: The proof derives the endpoint trace identity, separately credits the published spectral-spread bound, provides an attainable optimizer and discloses priority limitations.
scientific_limitations: Finite-dimensional positive-definite matrices only; two-eigenvalue first factor needed for sharp orbit classification.
The off-diagonal spectral-spread majorization itself is a published Li–Mathias theorem; only its quantitative near-geometric application is claimed.
Complete text of Franco–Gan–Kim (2025) was not accessible for priority comparison; equivalent earlier results remain possible.
No independent scientific audit or external validation.
title: Sharp fixed-spectrum trace dilation of the near-geometric endpoint for two-level positive matrices
